texts.preamble: Dr.D.Bhaskara Rao, Hyd Dt., vs State Of Telangana, Rep Pp And Anr., on 5 June, 2023 Hon'Ble Smt. Justice G. Anupama Chakravarthy Criminal Petition No.5041 of 2016 Order :
texts.facts: This criminal petition is filed seeking to quash the proceedings initiated by respondent No.2 against the petitioner/accused in C.C.No.2267 of 2015 on the file of XI Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Secunderabad, Hyderabad District. 2. Heard Sri M.S.Srinivas Ayyangar, learned Senior Counsel appearing for petitioner and Sri S. Ganesh, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for respondents. 3. The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner is the Managing Director of M/s.Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences Ltd. (hereinafter be referred as 'KIMS hospital'). The said hospital was operating 1800 bed multi super specialty hospital consisting of various wings/blocks known as (i) KIMS OT Pharmacy; (ii) KIMS IP pharmacy; (iii) KIMS Central Pharmacy (wholesale) and (iv) KIMS Central Pharmacy etc., certified by National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) and GAC, J National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers (NABH) Accreditations. It is also a certified International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 90001-2008 holder with over 50 medical and surgical disciplines. 4. The KIMS hospital has its registered office at Block-III, 11th Floor, D.No.1-8-31/1, Minister Road, Secunderabad, Hyderabad and was having valid drug licences in Form-20, 21 and 21(c) for its various blocks/wings of OT Pharmacy/IP pharmacy/Central pharmacy/Central pharmacy (wholesale)/KIMS pharmacy/KIMS Cathlab pharmacy etc., respectively issued by the Licencing Authority, Drugs Control Administration, Twin Cities-II, Hyderabad, Government of Telangana to sell, stock, exhibit, offer for sale or distribute drugs by retail other than those specified in Schedules C, C(1) and X of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. 5. The locations and licence particulars of the above said wings are as follows: " (i) The KIMS Central Pharmacy (Wholesale) bearing Drug Licence in Form - 21C bearing No.631/HD2/AP/2009, dated 14/10/2009 - GAC, J valid upto 13/10/2019 is situated at Ground Floor, Block - III. (iii) The KIMS Pharmacy bearing Drug Licence in Form - 20 bearing No.AP/24/05/2012-100153, dated 01/10/2015 - valid upto 22/08/2017 is situated at 1st Floor, Block - III. (iv) The KIMS Cathlab Pharmacy bearing Drug Licence in Form - 20 bearing No.TG/24/05/2015-8678, dated 05/08/2015 - valid upto 04/08/2020 is situated at 5th Floor, Block - III. (v) The KIMS OT Pharmacy bearing Drug Licence No.TG/24/03/2015-7135, dated 07/01/2016 - valid upto 11/06/2020 is situated at 6th & 7th Floor, Block - III. (vi) The KIMS IP Pharmacy bearing Drug Licence No.TG/24/05/2015-6320, dated 12/05/2015 - valid upto 11/05/2020 is situated at 11th Floor, Block - III." All the wings as mentioned above, are situated within premises of the KIMS hospital. 6. On 21.04.2015, Mrs. D. Swetha Bindu, the Drugs Inspector, Marredpally Zone (Sales), Secunderabad, Hyderabad District, the GAC, J respondent No.2/complainant herein, alleged to have received 'credible information' that certain drugs were stocked for sale other than at the licenced premises of the KIMS hospitals. She inspected the premises of the KIMS Hospital, at 11th Floor, wherein, the Pharmacy Wing of the KIMS hospitals i.e. KIMS IP Pharmacy Credit, along with Mrs.M. Sree Bindu, Panch witnesses Sri P.Kumara Swamy and Sri E. Mohan Reddy. At the time of purported inspection, the complainant/respondent No.2 herein and LW-3/Mrs.Janaki Rani Radham/Pharmacist and incharge of the said IP pharmacy wing of KIMS hospital were present. On being asked by respondent No.2/complainant, the said incharge Pharmacist informed that the petitioner/accused is the Managing Director of the KIMS hospitals and that the other Director Mr.Kameswara Rao Bhagawati was available at that point of time. Respondent No.2, after introducing herself to the incharge Pharmacist and on conducting inspection of the room, found that as many as 80 kinds of medicines are stocked in the iron racks for selling. It was found in the room a substance of "Pneumatic Internal Transport System". On further questioning by respondent GAC, J No.2, the Pharmacist has shown the drug licences in Form-21C, KIMS Inpatient Pharmacy, Door No.1-8-31/1, Block-I, 2nd floor, KIMS hospital, Minister Road, Secunderabad, Drug Lic.No.630/1102/AP/2009, valid upto 13/10/2019. On further questioning by respondent No.2 to show drug licence of inpatient pharmacy wing, the Pharmacist informed that there is no drug licence for the said address. On that, respondent No.2 informed the Pharmacist that stocking and selling of drugs without licence is an offence and further asked to show the Material Requisition Note (MRN) and Goods Issue Note (GIN). The Pharmacist has shown the copies of the MRN and GIN issued by the Central Stores of the KIMS hospital to the inpatient pharmacy credit wing. Further, respondent No.2/complainant has lifted two types of medicines for the purpose of analysis in terms of Form-17 and further, all the 80 kinds of medicines that were available in the Pharmacy Wing, the MRN and GIN and the copies of the pharmacy receipts were also taken into custody in terms of Form-16. The Dr.D.Bhaskara Rao, Hyd Dt., vs State Of Telangana, Rep Pp And Anr., on 5 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192001512/ 2 same were seized in the presence of panch witnesses. The information of seizure of 80 GAC, J varieties of medicines was given to the Director, Drugs Control Authority, Hyderabad on the same day. 7. On 22.04.2015, respondent No.2 has sent two varieties of sampled drugs to the Government Analyst, Drugs Control Laboratory, Hyderabad for the purpose of test/analysis and further intimated the seizure of drugs to the XI Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Secunderabad on the same day and sought orders from the Court for the safe custody of the seized products as per Section 23(5)(b) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act. The trial Court has allotted PI No.98 of 2015, dated 22.04.2015 and returned the seized property to LW-1 for safe custody, retaining original Form-16, original panchanama and documents. On 24.04.2015, respondent No.2 has issued notices under Sections 18A and 22(1)(cc) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, requesting to furnish the alleged details pertaining to the drugs seized from the premises of KIMS hospital, for which, the Pharmacist of the hospital has sought time vide letters dated 07.05.2015 and 06.06.2015. On 01.08.2015, the Pharmacist of KIMS hospital has issued reply furnishing the copies of the drug GAC, J licences in Forms - 20 and 21 and also the copies of the goods issue note and pharmacy receipts of the drugs seized, which were raised in the name of KIMS IP pharmacy of KIMS hospital at Block No.1, 2nd Floor, Door No.1-8-31/1, Minister Road, Secunderabad. On 27.04.2015, respondent No.2 has submitted a report again to the Director, DCA, Hyderabad, informing about the seizure from the petitioner-hospital vide proceedings dated 17.08.2015 and instructed to complete the investigation and file complaint in the Court of law. Pursuant to the inspection report of respondent No.2 dated 21.04.2015, the incharge Assistant Director (Twin Cities-II), Drugs Control Administration, Hyderabad has addressed letter dated 23.04.2015 to KIMS inpatient pharmacy, invoking the provisions of Rule 66(1) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules and issued show cause notice calling upon to explain within a period of Seven days from the date of receipt of the letter as to why their drug licences in Forms-21, 20-B and 21-B should not be suspended, failing which, it would be construed that there is no explanation to offer and action will be taken. GAC, J 8. Accordingly, the management, KIMS hospital was constrained to approach the Assistant Director and it was further compelled to obtain three licences in Form-21 dated 12.05.2015, 05.08.2015 and 07.01.2016 in the name of - (i) M/s. KIMS IP Pharmacy in the premises of KIMS hospital, situated at Block-III, 11th floor; (ii) KIMS Cathlab Pharmacy in the premises of KIMS hospital, situated at Block-III, 5th floor and (iii) M/s. KIMS OT Pharmacy in the premises of KIMS hospital, situated at Block-III, 6th and 7th floors, all with D.No.1-8-31/1, Minister Road, Secunderabad, Hyderabad. 9. On 05.09.2015, the complainant/respondent No.2 received test analysis report for two sampled drugs in Form-13, dated 24.08.2015 for the drugs 'Glan Pan Injection' and 'Citralka Syrup', opining that those drugs were of standard quality. Later, respondent No.2 lodged complaint before the XI Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Secunderabad on 30.09.2015 against the petitioner for the offences punishable under Section 27(b)(ii) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, which are the impugned proceedings. The learned Magistrate took cognizance for the said offences on GAC, J 14.12.2015 and issued summons to the petitioner to appear before the Court on 10.02.2016. It is the contention of the learned counsel for petitioner that the panchanamas drawn by respondent No.2 are specific and self-explanatory, which clearly reveal that the drugs were stocked for sale at 11th floor of KIMS hospital and they are found in one room of East facing entrance. On the right side of the room, there is one fire alarm, fire exit on left side and lift at opposite to room entrance. It is also the contention of the learned counsel that respondent No.2 along with the panch witnesses, arrived at the premises of the hospital at 4.20 p.m. on 21.04.2015 and they also found the Pharmacist/Janaki Rani and on being asked, she informed about the Managing Director and also about the Director, who were available.
texts.arguments: 11. In support of his contentions, the learned counsel for petitioner has relied on the following judgments: (1) In Aneeta Hada v. Godfather Travels and Tours Pvt. Ltd.1, wherein, it is held: (2012) 5 SCC 661 GAC, J "The core issue that has emerged in these two appeals is whether the company could have been made liable for prosecution without being impleaded as an accused and whether the directors could have been prosecuted for offences punishable under the aforesaid provisions without the company being arrayed as an accused. Being aggrieved by the said order, she invoked the jurisdiction of the High Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing of the criminal proceeding and the High Court, considering the scope of Sections 138 and 139 of the Act and various other factors, opined that the ground urged would be in the sphere of defence of the accused and would not strengthen the edifice for quashing of the proceeding." The decision in Anil Hada (supra) is overruled with the qualifier as stated in paragraph. (2) In Himanshu v. B. The appellant had signed the cheque as a Director of the company and for and on its behalf. (3) In Hindustan Unilever Limited v. State of Madhya Pradesh3, wherein, it is held; (2019) 3 SCC 797 (2020) 10 SCC 751 GAC, J "A three-Judge Bench of this Court in Aneeta Hada v. Godfather Travels & Tours Private Limited11 considered the question of conviction of the Directors in the absence of the Company in proceedings under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 as also in the proceedings under Information Technology Act, 2000. This Court held that Section 141 of the NI Act dealing with offences by companies contemplates that every person who at the time the offence was committed, was in charge of, and was responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the company, as well as the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly. From the aforesaid pronouncements, the principle that can be culled out is that it is the bounden duty of the court to ascertain for what purpose the legal fiction has been created. The words "as well as" have to be understood in the context. xx xx xx (4) In Dayle De'souza v. Shivamurthy and Another. The relevant portion of the judgment reads thus: "6. The judgment of the High Court has been questioned on two grounds. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that firstly, the appellant could not be prosecuted without the company being named as an accused. The cheque was issued by the company and was signed by the appellant as its Director. Secondly, it was urged that the observation of the High Court that the company can now be proceeded against in the complaint is misconceived. The learned counsel submitted that the offence under Section 138 is complete only upon the issuance of a notice of demand and the failure of payment within the prescribed period. A decision of a three-Judge Bench of this Court in Aneeta Hada v. Godfather Travels & Tours (P) Ltd. governs the area of dispute. The issue which fell for consideration was whether an authorised signatory of a company would be liable for prosecution under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 without the company being arraigned as an accused. Applying the same proposition of law as laid down in Aneeta Hada (supra), this Court in Hindustan Unilever Limited v. State of Madhya Pradesh applying pari materia provision in Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, held that: "23. Clause (a) of sub-section (1) of Section 17 of the Act makes the person nominated to be in charge of and responsible to the company for the conduct of business and the company shall be guilty of the offences under clause (b) of sub-section (1) of Section 17 of the Act. Therefore, there is no material distinction between Section 141 of the NI Act and Section 17 of the Act which makes the company as well as the nominated person to be held guilty of the offences and/or liable to be proceeded and punished accordingly. Since the Company was not convicted by the trial court, we find that the finding of the High Court to revisit the Dr.D.Bhaskara Rao, Hyd Dt., vs State Of Telangana, Rep Pp And Anr., on 5 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192001512/ 6 judgment will be unfair to the appellant-nominated person who has been facing GAC, J trial for more than last 30 years. 13.
